description: This bar chart, titled “Researcher Location,” illustrates the number of hateful communication datasets published annually from 2012 to 2022, categorized by the geographic location of the researchers involved. The vertical axis, labeled “Number of datasets,” uses a logarithmic scale ranging from 10⁰ (1) to 10² (100), with major gridlines at 1, 10, and 100. The horizontal axis represents the year, spanning from 2012 to 2022. Six researcher locations are color-coded in the legend: “Other” (blue), “UK” (red), “USA” (orange), “IT” (purple), “IN” (green), and “DE” (brown). Each year displays a group of up to six bars, one per location, with bar height indicating the count of datasets. In early years (2012–2015), only a few datasets are shown, mostly from “USA” and “Other.” From 2016 onward, dataset counts rise significantly, with “Other” consistently contributing the most datasets each year, peaking at over 100 in 2021. “USA” and “DE” also show strong growth, with “USA” reaching nearly 50 in 2021 and “DE” exceeding 20 in 2020 and 2021. “UK,” “IT,” and “IN” show more modest contributions, with “IN” reaching around 20 in 2021 and “IT” peaking at about 10 in 2019 and 2021. In 2022, “Other” remains highest (~30), followed by “IN” (~10) and “UK” (~10), while “IT” drops to ~2. The chart visually emphasizes the dominance of researchers categorized as “Other” and the growing international participation in dataset creation over time.
